body.p: Reconsideration of the above-identified application in view of the amendments above and the remarks following is respectfully requested.
Claims 1-10 are in this Application. Claims 2 and 6 -10 have been cancelled. New claim 11 has been added herewith.
Claim Objections

Claims 9-10 are objected to because of in claim 9, line 4, "the camera head" should be changed to --a camera head- and in claim 10, lines 2-4, "the sample arm and the reference arm are arranged in the second housing or in the camera head." should be changed to --a sample arm and a reference arm are arranged in a second housing or in the camera head.-. Applicant cancelled these claims and therefore this rejection is believed to be moot.

Claims 1-3, 7 and 10 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as being anticipated by Dave et al. (US 2004/0126048 Al), hereafter Dave. Claim 4 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Dave in view of Lam et al. (US 2017/0196459 Al), hereafter Lam). Claim 5 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Dave in view of Pan et al. (US 2010/0280315 Al), hereafter Pan. Claims 6 and 8-9 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Dave in view of Wax et al. (US 2019/0368861 Al), hereafter Wax.
Applicant amended Claim 1 to recite features from original claims 2 and 8 to 10.

The claimed invention's specific arrangement of the reference arm and sample arm together in a camera head, with non-polarization-maintaining fibers leading to both arms, is not suggested by Dave. Dave shows a generic arrangement where the reference arm and sample arm are depicted separately, with the sample arm typically in the lower part of the figures and the reference arm in the upper part. This separation would not have suggested combining these arms in a single camera head as in the claimed invention.
Furthermore, Dave would have led a person skilled in the art to use polarization- maintaining fibers in both the reference and sample arms, as these converge for example
at a light combiner. This is in contrast to the claimed invention, which specifically uses non-polarization-maintaining fibers for these arms up to the light combiner.

The claimed arrangement provides several advantages as it allows for a more compact design by housing both arms together and reduces cost and complexity by using non-polarization-maintaining fibers where possible. It also maintains polarization information where it's most critical - after the light combiner.

These benefits would not have been obvious from the teachings of Dave or similar prior art. The claimed invention represents a non-obvious step beyond the state of the art, providing a unique solution that balances performance, cost, and compactness in a way not previously achieved.

Moreover, while Claims 1 and 2 are rejected based on Dave, Claims 6 and 8 are rejected based on the teaching of Dave in view of Wax. In particular, Examiner contends that it would been obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art before the effective filling day of the claimed invention to modify the device of Dave by including the first interferometer part is assigned to a power supply unit, the first interferometer part is accommodated in a first housing, comprising electronic components and a power supply unit, the second interferometer part is accommodated in a second housing comprising the camera head (as taught by Wax) for several advantages such as: allow to provide independent power supply to the OCT scan device thus allow to provide a portable device increasing the efficiency of the device, also the housing provide protection to the internal elements from external elements as dust and water ([0049], Wax).

The amended claim now specifies that the second housing comprises not only the second interferometer part and camera head, but also a sample arm and a reference arm (which may also be in the camera head itself which is in the second housing). Neither Dave nor Wax teach or suggest including both the sample arm and reference arm together with the second interferometer part in a second housing separate from the first housing containing the first interferometer part. This particular configuration of components between the two housings is not disclosed or suggested by the prior art of record.

The amended claim further specifies that the flexible light guide comprises two polarization-maintaining light-guiding fibers connected to each other, wherein the respective crystal axes of the fibers are arranged tilted by 900 relative to each other. While

Dave discusses using polarization-maintaining fibers, it does not disclose the specific configuration of two fibers connected with their crystal axes tilted 90° relative to each other as now claimed. This particular arrangement of the polarization-maintaining fibers provides a novel and non-obvious structure not taught by the prior art of record.

The combination of elements as arranged in the amended claim - with the specific division of components between the first and second housings, along with the particular configuration of the polarization-maintaining fibers - is not suggested by Dave, Wax, or their combination. The claimed arrangement appears to provide advantages in terms of flexibility, polarization control, and component isolation that would not have been obvious to one of ordinary skill in the art based on the cited references.

For these reasons, the particular combination and arrangement of elements as now claimed is not taught or suggested by Dave, Wax, or their combination. The examiner would need to identify new prior art or provide further reasoning to maintain a rejection of the amended claim.
Reservation of Rights

In the interest of clarity and brevity, not every assertion made by the Examiner in the Office Action may have been addressed. Failure to address every assertion does not constitute an admission of or acquiescence in it. All arguments not made in connection with this response, inter alia, such as the right to challenge or rebut any tacit or explicit characterization of any reference or of any of the present claims, the right to challenge or rebut any asserted factual or legal basis of any of the rejections, or the right to assert co- ownership of any cited reference, are reserved. It is not admitted that any of the cited references or any other references of record are relevant to the present claims, or that they constitute prior art. To the extent that any rejection or assertion is based upon the Examiner's personal knowledge, rather than any objective evidence of record as manifested by a cited prior art reference, timely objection to such reliance on Official Notice is made, and all rights to request that the Examiner provide support of such assertion are reserved. All rights to pursue any cancelled claims in a subsequent patent
application claiming the benefit of priority of the present patent application, and to request rejoinder of any withdrawn claim are similarly reserved.
No Disclaimers or Disavowals

Although the present response may include amendments to the application or claims, or characterizations of claim scope or referenced art, Applicant does not concede that previously pending claims in this application are not patentable over the cited references. Rather, any amendments or characterizations are being made to expedite the issuance. Applicant reserves the right to pursue at a later date any previously pending or other broader or narrower claims that relate to subject matter supported by the instant application, including subject matter specifically disclaimed herein or by any prior prosecution. Accordingly, reviewers of this application, or any parent, child or related prosecution history should not infer that Applicant has made any disclaimers or disavowals of any subject matter supported by the instant application.
In view of the above amendments and remarks it is respectfully submitted that the claims are now in condition for allowance. A prompt notice of allowance is respectfully and earnestly solicited.

While the above amendments and/or remarks are believed to be sufficient to overcome the Examiner's rejections, any omissions as to assertions by the Examiner or certain requirements that may be applicable to such rejections (e.g., assertions regarding dependent claims, whether a reference constitutes prior art, whether references are legally combinable for obviousness purposes) is not an admission that such assertions are accurate or such requirements have been met. Applicant reserves the right to analyze and dispute such positions in the future.
